source_text: De exitu plane passionis ejus ambigitis, negantes passionem crucis in Christum praedicatam, et argumentantes insuper non esse credendum, ut ad id genus mortis exposuerit Deus filium suum, quod ipse dixit: Maledictus omnis homo qui pependit in ligno. Sed hujus maledictionis sensum antecedit rerum probatio. Dicit enim in Deuteronomio: Si autem fuerit in aliquo delictum, ita ut judicium mortis sit, et morietur, et suspendetis eum in ligno. Sed et sepultura sepelietis cum ipsa die: quoniam maledictus a Deo est omnis qui suspensus fuerit in ligno, et non inquinabitis terram quam Dominus Deus tuus dabit tibi in sortem. Igitur non in hanc passionem Christum maledixit; sed distinctionem fecit, ut qui in aliquo delicto judicium mortis habuisset et moreretur suspensus in ligno, hic maledictus a Deo esset, quia propter merita delictorum suorum suspenderetur in ligno. Alioquin Christus, qui dolum de ore suo locutus non est, quique omnem justitiam et humilitatem exhibuit; et ut supra de eo praedictum memoravimus, non pro meritis suis in id genus mortis expositus est, sed ut ea quae praedicta sunt a prophetis, per vos ei obventura implerentur, sicut in Psalmis ipse Spiritus Christi jam canebat, dicens: Retribuebant mihi mala pro bonis, et: Quae non rapueram, tunc exsolvebam; Exterminaverunt manus meas et pedes; et: Miserunt in potum meum fel, et in siti mea potaverunt me aceto; et, Super vestem meam miserunt sortem; sicuti caetera quae in illum commissuri essetis, praedicta sunt. Quae quidem omnia ipso perpessus, non pro actu suo aliquo malo passus est, sed ut Scripturae implerentur de ore prophetarum. Et utique sacramentum passionis ipsius figurari in praedicationibus oportuerat; quantoque incredibile, tanto magis scandalum futurum, si nude praedicaretur; quantoque magnificum, tanto magis obumbrandum, ut difficultas intellectus gratiam Dei quaereret. Itaque in primis Isaac cum a patre hostia duceretur, et lignum ipsi sibi portaret, Christi exitum jam tunc denotabat, in victimam concessi a patre, lignum passionis suae bajulantis.
pass_a_gloss: You are indeed doubting about the outcome of His passion, denying the passion of the cross preached in Christ, and arguing furthermore that it is not to be believed that God exposed His Son to this kind of death, because He Himself said: Cursed is every man who hangs on a tree. But the sense of this curse is preceded by the proof of the facts. For He says in Deuteronomy: But if there is a sin in someone, so that the judgment of death is, and he dies, and you hang him on a tree, but you will bury him with the same day: because cursed by God is every one who has been hanged on a tree, and you will not defile the land which the Lord your God gives to you as a possession. Therefore, God did not curse Christ in this passion; but He made a distinction, so that whoever had the judgment of death in some sin and died hanged on a tree, this one was cursed by God, because he was hanged on a tree because of the merits of his sins. Otherwise, Christ, who spoke no deceit from His mouth, and who exhibited all justice and humility; and as we remembered above, was predicted about Him, was not exposed to this kind of death because of His merits, but so that the things which were predicted by the prophets would happen to Him through you, just as in the Psalms the Spirit of Christ Himself was singing, saying: They were repaying me evil for good, and: What I had not plundered, then I was paying; They were destroying my hands and feet; and: They were putting gall in my drink, and in my thirst they were making me drink vinegar; and, They were casting lots over my garment; just as the other things which you were going to commit against Him were predicted. Which things, indeed, having suffered them, He did not suffer because of some evil act of His, but so that the Scriptures might be fulfilled from the mouth of the prophets. And certainly, the sacrament of His passion had to be prefigured in the preachings; and the more incredible, the more it was going to be a scandal, if it were preached nakedly; and the more magnificent, the more it was going to be obscured, so that the difficulty of understanding might seek the grace of God. And so, first of all, Isaac, when he was being led as a sacrifice by his father, and was carrying the wood for himself, was already indicating the outcome of Christ, in a victim yielded by the father, carrying the wood of His passion.

pass_b_english: You are actually doubting how His passion turned out, denying that the cross's suffering was preached in Christ, and arguing further that God could not have handed His Son over to this kind of death, since He Himself declared: "Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree" (Deuteronomy 21:22-23). But the proof of the facts comes before the sense of that curse. Deuteronomy says: "If someone has committed a capital offense and is put to death, and you hang his body on a tree, you must not leave it there overnight; you must bury him that same day, because anyone hung on a tree is under God's curse, and you must not defile the land the Lord your God is giving you as an inheritance" (Deuteronomy 21:22-23). Therefore God did not curse Christ in this passion; He drew a distinction, so that whoever had a death sentence for some sin and died hanging on a tree — that person was cursed by God, because he was hung on a tree due to the merits of his own sins. Christ, however, spoke no deceit from His mouth and displayed all justice and humility; as we recalled above, He was foretold not to be handed over to this death because of His own merits, but so that the things the prophets predicted would happen to Him through you would be fulfilled — just as the Spirit of Christ Himself was already singing in the Psalms: "They repay me evil for good" (Psalms 35:12); "I am forced to restore what I did not steal"; "They pierce my hands and feet"; "They put gall in my food and give me vinegar for my thirst" (Psalms 69:21); "They cast lots for my garment" — just as the other things you were going to commit against Him were foretold. He suffered all these things, yet not because of any evil act of His own, but so that the Scriptures from the prophets' mouths might be fulfilled. And indeed, the mystery of His passion had to be prefigured in the prophecies; the more incredible it was, the more it would become a scandal if preached plainly; the more magnificent, the more it had to be veiled, so that the difficulty of understanding it would drive people to seek God's grace. Thus, first of all, when Isaac was led as a sacrifice by his father and carried the wood himself, he was already signifying Christ's outcome: a victim yielded by the Father, bearing the wood of His own passion.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass B correctly identifies and adds the required inline scripture citations (Deuteronomy 21:22-23, Psalms 35:12, Psalms 69:21) which were alluded to in the Latin but not explicitly numbered. Pass B's handling of the Psalm quotes (e.g., 'They pierce my hands and feet' for 'Exterminaverunt manus meas et pedes') is a valid idiomatic translation of the sense. Pass A and B are consistent with the source.
